correctness.rationale: Let F=min(1,sum x_i) and M=max x_i. For all x in [0,1]^n, 0<=F-M<=1-1/n, so Zadeh formula M attains error d. Rational-shifted clipped maximum min(1,M+d/2) in the non-expansive language attains error d/2. A one-world reflexive Kripke model reduces arbitrary modal syntax to propositional functions: non-expansive operations are all 1-Lipschitz in ||.||_infty. Between all-zero input and all-1/n input F rises by 1 over distance 1/n, proving any such approximant error >=(1-1/n)/2. At equality both endpoint inequalities saturate and force g(t,...,t)=t+d/2 for t∈[0,1/n]. In plain Zadeh without intermediate constants, on diagonal 0<t<1/2 every formula is identically one of 0,t,1-t,1; continuity and required error below d force 0 or t near zero, giving lower bound d at t=1/n for n>2 or t->1/2 for n=2. Full Łukasiewicz expresses F exactly. The lower bounds hold for every allowed modal depth because the singleton model is included among all pointed models. A separately implemented exact-rational grid checked n=2,3,4 and attained both sharp errors.

value.rationale: Strong n-ary Łukasiewicz disjunction is a canonical excluded connective of the Zadeh and intermediate non-expansive bases. The theorem gives sharp all-n, all-model approximation thresholds, a factor-two quantitative expressivity distinction, modal-depth irrelevance, and a rigidity constraint on every optimal nonexpansive translator.
